slides.heading: What it is
paras: The two canonical building blocks of academic HFT: a closed-form model for where to quote (Avellaneda-Stoikov) and a statistical model for when trades cluster (Hawkes).
slides.alt: DejaViewed carousel, slide 2 of 8. The idea. What it is. The two canonical building blocks of academic HFT: a closed-form model for where to quote (Avellaneda-Stoikov) and a statistical model for when trades cluster (Hawkes). From @heidioftheeast.

slides.heading: What a pro would do that you didn't ask for
paras: A market-making quant would not trust the closed-form spread until it is calibrated in the right units: σ and k must be expressed per price unit and time unit consistent with the tick size…

slides.heading: 3 steps that matter most
steps: Ground truth: verify the repo against the paper
Make sure the formulas and code agree before anything is built on them.

Validate against oracles and write the gap report

slides.heading: How you know it worked
items: The AS 2008 paper's inventory versus symmetric strategy table, reproduced within sampling error from the repo's parameters.
The time-rescaling theorem: KS test of Hawkes residuals against Exp(1) passing in at least 70% of held-out windows.
